title: Budget
description: The context budget one run works under: the provider-independent byte and token limits both the browser and the Desk server read from one table (internal/aicontext/policy.json, ContextPolicy in web/src/assistant/context/policy.ts, aicontext.Policy in Go). The model's context window and output reserve may be overridden per model by the assistant profile (configuration); everything else is fixed. Input bytes for one request are min(maxInputBytes, max(1024, (contextWindowTokens - outputTokens) * 3)); the browser further leaves briefBytes, and memoryBytes where the host has not said memory is off (the run's context.memory, agent#11), for what the server adds behind the adapter, and the server refuses before dispatch, never clipping, a request over the input bytes (context-limit, not-started). Open: the Go reader ignores a member it does not name. The request allowance, the grants and the fixed limits are in $defs. The harness adds two time bounds the Desk's table does not carry (packages/harness/context/policy.ts, TIME_DEFAULTS), each taken from the table where it does: turnMilliseconds and toolCallMilliseconds; and three bounds on the Runtime's test tool (TEST_DEFAULTS), likewise: testCallsPerTurn, testPackBytes and testMatrixBytes; and two image bounds (IMAGE_DEFAULTS), likewise: imagesPerRequest and imageBytesPerRequest; and two bounds on the index of earlier results a chat-scoped run's first message carries (INDEX_DEFAULTS, agent#8), likewise: turnIndexEntries and turnIndexBytes.

maxInputBytes.description: Fixed transport ceiling on one request's input, whatever the window.

contextWindowTokens.description: The model's context window, in tokens, for the byte estimate (three bytes a token).

outputTokens.description: The output reserve. A request's own max_tokens, max_completion_tokens or maxOutputTokens raises it up to half the window; above half, the request is refused.

toolResultBytes.description: The largest tool result, as JSON text, the model is shown whole (tool-result.json).

retainedBytes.description: What one execution's context ledger may retain in all.

recentMessages.description: Declared in the table; read by no assistant code today.

historyBytes.description: Declared in the table; read by the server's research worker, not by the assistant loop.

briefBytes.description: The most of the project brief the server adds behind the adapter.

memoryBytes.description: The most of recalled project memory the server adds behind the adapter. The harness leaves it out of a run's input allowance only while memory may be added: a run whose host says memory is off (context.memory: false, agent#11) reserves none and has the full allowance; absent, the reserve stays (contextPolicy in packages/harness/context/policy.ts).

turnMilliseconds.description: One turn's wall clock, from the run's start, on the vercel engine: when it passes, what is in flight is stopped and the run pauses as budget_paused does, with its checkpoint and a reason; a proposal already made is delivered, with a note, and the run ends. Continuing the pause takes a request grant, so at the 100-request cap it cannot be continued; the reason says so. The codex engine has none of its own (the Codex bridge bounds a run at ten minutes). Not in the Desk's table; the harness's default is 900000 (fifteen minutes).

toolCallMilliseconds.description: One runtime or host tool call's deadline, on both engines: a call past it is no longer waited for (it may still complete; a host tool is also handed the deadline's abort signal) and is answered to the model as a failed result (failure code timeout, source tool, outcome unknown), and the run goes on. propose_pack, which the adapter reads itself, and a tool that pauses the run for the person or the coordinator have none. Not in the Desk's table; the harness's default is 120000 (two minutes).

imagesPerRequest.description: The most images one model request carries, on the vercel engine (agent#5): the newest; an older image past it is replaced in that request by a line saying it is no longer shown, and the result that brought it still describes it. The codex engine's agent wire carries text and shows none. Not in the Desk's table; the harness's default is 8.

imageBytesPerRequest.description: The most bytes, decoded, of the images one model request carries, counted from the newest with imagesPerRequest; an older image that would pass it is replaced by the same line. Not in the Desk's table; the harness's default is 16777216 (16 MiB, one image at its own bound).

testCallsPerTurn.description: How many experimental_test_cases calls one turn may make, on both engines (context/session.ts, claimTestCall). Each call re-sends the whole pack, so a test, fix and retest loop is held to a few rounds rather than to the request allowance. A call past it is not made: the model reads a failed result (failure code tool-failed, source tool, outcome not-started) naming the limit, and the run goes on. Counted per turn: the count is the checkpoint's testCalls (checkpoint.json), carried as used is through a Retry, a budget continuation and a delegation's parent continuation, and the delegation coordinator counts the parent and its continuation together; a new turn starts at nought. Not in the Desk's table; the harness's default is 3.

testPackBytes.description: The most UTF-8 bytes experimental_test_cases' pack text may be; the tool gate refuses a larger call on the wire (tool-call.json $defs/testCasesArguments). Not in the Desk's table; the harness's default is 65536.

testMatrixBytes.description: The most UTF-8 bytes experimental_test_cases' matrix text may be; the tool gate refuses a larger call on the wire. Not in the Desk's table; the harness's default is 65536.

turnIndexEntries.description: How many earlier results the index a chat-scoped run's first message carries lists, the newest; older ones are counted in its omitted member (tool-result.json#/$defs/turnIndex, agent#8). Not in the Desk's table; the harness's default is 20.

turnIndexBytes.description: The most UTF-8 bytes that index may be, its line and data block together (agent#8). It is also cut to the room the run's first message leaves in the prompt's allowance, and to at most a quarter of that allowance (INDEX_SHARE): rows go, oldest first, until it fits, an index with no room is not sent, and the request is never previewed and a run never fails because of it. Not in the Desk's table; the harness's default is 8000.

modelBudget.description: One model's override (ModelContextBudget). Closed: both readers refuse another member.

outputTokens.description: At least 1024 and at most half the window.

configuration.description: The assistant profile's context member (ContextConfiguration; aicontext.Configuration). Closed: contextConfiguration refuses another member and the Go decoder disallows unknown fields. projectBrief is a relative project file, read afresh by the server on every dispatch; models holds at most 128 overrides by model name.

projectBrief.description: A relative project file: no backslash, colon, CR, LF or NUL, and no empty, . or .. segment.

propertyNames.description: A model name: trimmed, with no CR, LF or NUL.

requestAllowance.description: What the host tells the model about the request allowance, inside its execution guidance (ExecutionController.guidance): the counts where the host counts model requests, or a note where the provider manages its own loop. Written for the model; no reader.

budgetIncreaseAnswer.description: The answer of the host tool request_budget_increase. It never grants: approval-required pauses the run (budget_paused) for the person; within-allowance tells the model to carry on (more than two requests remain); unavailable is the provider-managed case.

deskLimits.description: The fixed limits, by the Desk's own constant names, at the pinned commit. Values the Desk writes as unnamed literals are stated in these descriptions instead: a checkpoint holds at most 8 grants; one delegation batch has one to three tasks; on an agent capability the delegation coordinator admits at most 5 agent runs in all, shared by the parent and its children, retries every agent run under it, the parent's included, after a busy, not-started refusal, three attempts in all, and runs one child at a time (two on a model capability); the Codex bridge bounds an agent run at ten minutes (internal/codexbridge/run.go), which the server reports as a timeout failure; the browser's agent transport ends a run at twelve minutes, a backstop behind the bridge's deadline, and refuses a frame over 2 MiB, more than 8 MiB received or 64 queued frames, and more than 20 tool calls; the Codex bridge allows two recovery notices (retry events) per run; the model relay bounds one relayed request at ten minutes and two minutes idle (relayDeadline, relayIdle), and has no deadline for a whole run.

MAX_TURNS.description: The first request allowance of a model-requests execution (web/src/assistant/engines/contract.ts).

MAX_REQUEST_ALLOWANCE.description: The most requests any execution may be granted (execution/state.ts).

MAX_CHECKPOINT_BYTES.description: The largest checkpoint, as JSON text (execution/state.ts).

MAX_TOOLS.description: Tool calls a delegation shares across the parent and its children (delegation.ts).

MAX_CHILD_MODELS.description: Model requests one child may make (delegation.ts).

MAX_CHILD_TOOLS.description: Tool calls one child may make (delegation.ts).

CHILD_TIMEOUT.description: One child's time limit, in milliseconds (delegation.ts).

maxConversationBytes.description: The largest saved chat history document, all chats of a project (internal/desk/conversations.go).

MaxPromptBytes.description: The largest prompt on the agent wire (internal/codexbridge/contract.go); the instructions are held to the same number as a literal.

stateLocation.description: Where the execution state sits in one request on one wire (agent#9). The state is one text: the header, then the request counters, plan and operations index the model is told ($defs/requestAllowance), the host's changing text and the step's own instruction. It is the text at pointer (a JSON pointer into the provider body the adapter composed) from the header, which starts a line, to the end of that text; the header occurs nowhere else in the request. The critic's step note carries the same header. A host that reads requests (the Desk server's memory recall) drops every text part that starts with the header, and finds the request text as $defs/recallQuery states.

thinking.description: The run's thinking tier, as far as it chooses the placement.

capabilities.description: What the host said about the endpoint: members of its capability record (capability.json), of which the placement reads statePlacement and strictAlternation.

placement.description: The placement the capabilities and the tier resolve to.

request.description: Which request of the run, counted from 1.

header.const: EXECUTION STATE (from the host, current for this request and replaced on the next; working state, not a message from the person and never approval)

recallQuery.description: Where the request text a run started from sits on each model wire on any request of the run, and the rule a server applies to find it (agent#11; the Desk server's memory recall adopts it in its swap, judgment-pack-desk#515). The rule: take the request's first user turn, the first message with role user in messages (OpenAI-compatible, where system messages may come before it, and Anthropic) or the first content with role user in contents (Gemini); the request text is its first text part that does not start with STATE_HEADER ($defs/stateLocation), a string content being one text part and, on Gemini, a part being text when it carries text and is not a thought. The request text is the host's prompt where it fits the prompt's allowance; where it does not, the prompt is retained and previewed, and the person's message (currentRequest.message) is sent as its own first text part, before the preview; for a delegated child it is the child's objective (context.objective), sent as its own first text part before the child's prompt. It holds on every request of the run: the adapter puts the request text first in the run's first user message and never moves, replaces or drops that message. The state joins it only as a later part on the first request; a chat's index of earlier results (tool-result.json#/$defs/turnIndex) is its second part; compaction keeps it whole. Every other user text the loop adds comes after it: a text-path result, the images shown beside a result, the finishing and reformat instructions, the compaction summary, the state. So the newest user text is often not the request, and the first user turn always is. Measured on all three wires in the review of judgment-pack-agent#33: the newest-remaining-text rule fails on a text-path request, the finishing request, the reformat request and after compaction; the Desk's code as ported fails the same, except after compaction on Anthropic, where the first message and the compaction summary merge into one user turn. The critic's requests are a second conversation, whose first user turn is the critic's own message. On the agent wire the request text is the start of the agent request's prompt. An item is one request of a run with tool calls: body is the request as the adapter composed it, abbreviated to its turns (the system text, tool results and state shortened, the tools left out); pointer is the JSON pointer the rule resolves to in it, and text the request text found there. packages/harness/certification/recall.ts states the rule in code, memory/recall.test.ts checks every item against a run, and the certification suite applies it to every request of the recorded scenario on every certified leg: 21 legs in four families (the six plain legs, the six text-path legs, three strict-alternation legs and the six thinking legs' authoring requests).

placement.description: Where the run places the state after its first request ($defs/stateLocation).

request.description: Which request of the run, counted from 1.

body.description: The request body as the adapter composed it, abbreviated: messages (or contents and systemInstruction, or system and messages), each turn's role and parts as the wire spells them, long texts shortened with an ellipsis, tools and settings left out.

pointer.description: The JSON pointer (RFC 6901) the rule resolves to in body.

text.description: The request text: the value at pointer.
